    "25014687": {
      "label": "CLARINET",
      "design": "RCT",
      "arms": "Lanreotide vs placebo",
      "result": "Primary endpoint met: median PFS not reached vs 18.0 mo (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73); 24-mo PFS 65.1% vs 33.0%; no OS or QoL difference",
      "caution": "96% stable; grade 2 HR 0.45 (0.22–0.91), pancreatic HR 0.58 (0.32–1.04); no predictive cutoff",
      "quotes": [
        "204 patients with unresectable or metastatic, somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 (Ki-67 under 10%) non-functioning enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours randomised at 48 centres in 14 countries between June 2006 and April 2013: 101 to lanreotide Autogel 120 mg and 103 to placebo, with 96% having had no documented progression in the preceding 3 to 6 months.",
        "CLARINET establishes that lanreotide 120 mg delays radiographic progression in somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, with a hazard ratio of 0.47 (95% CI 0.30–0.73) and 65.1% versus 33.0% progression-free at 24 months, and it does so across hepatic tumour volumes above and below 25%. What it does not establish is that this changes anything a patient feels or how long they live: no statistically significant difference in overall survival or quality of life was demonstrated, the population was non-functioning and 96% radiographically stable at entry, and subgroup estimates do not establish a predictive grade threshold; grade 2 HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The placebo arm ran a median 18.0 months without progression, which is the figure to carry into any discussion of whether to start treatment now or watch, and the hepatic-volume subgroup everyone quotes was collapsed from five prespecified categories to two after the data were in.",
        "The subgroup that matters most for liver-directed decisions is a post hoc construction. Hepatic tumour volume was prespecified in five categories whose estimated hazard ratios ranged from 0.24 to 0.54, and was collapsed after the fact into a dichotomy at 25%. The conclusion that the effect holds irrespective of hepatic tumour volume rests on that simplification, as the paper's own table footnote states.",
        "CLARINET’s grade 2 subgroup HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The HR 0.58 (0.32–1.04) belongs to the pancreatic-primary subgroup. Subgroup estimates do not establish differential benefit by grade or primary site.",
        "CLARINET subgroup estimates are exploratory: the pancreatic subgroup HR was 0.58 (95% CI 0.32–1.04), hepatic tumour volume >25% HR 0.45 (0.23–0.88), and grade 2 HR 0.45 (0.22–0.91). These are different strata. The estimates do not establish a predictive primary-site, grade or liver-volume cutoff.",
        "The whole benefit is radiographic. Overall survival did not differ, EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status did not differ, and the population was non-functioning by design so there were no hormonal symptoms to improve. Crossover is invoked to explain the survival null without any crossover numbers or a sensitivity analysis being presented.",
        "The size of the effect is unknown because the trial ended before it could be measured. Median progression-free survival was not reached with lanreotide within the 96-week fixed study duration, so the delay is known only to exceed the observation window, and the 96-week design cannot address how long treatment should continue.",
        "Progression-free survival and time to tumour progression return the identical 18.0-month placebo median from different event counts (60 against 58), which shows the median sits in a sparse region of the curve where two events make no difference to the estimate.",
        "The chromogranin A result is reported on 64 of 101 and 64 of 103 patients, roughly two-thirds of each arm, with no account of the missing third, and it is a biochemical change in a non-functioning tumour population where it carries no symptomatic meaning.",
        "Enrolment required somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy uptake of grade 2 or higher within the previous 6 months, so the trial selected the patients most likely to respond and says nothing about receptor-poor disease, which is precisely the group in whom embolisation, chemotherapy or resection is being weighed.",
        "The trial excluded any prior radionuclide therapy at any time, chemoembolisation or chemotherapy within 6 months, and more than 15 days of previous somatostatin analogue. The cohort is therefore essentially naive to liver-directed treatment, and nothing in the result informs sequencing with embolisation, radioembolisation or PRRT.",
        "The discussion raises the obvious reading of its own data, that an 18-month placebo median supports watchful waiting, and sets it aside on the ground that the study examined prevention of progression. That is a restatement of the trial's design, not an answer to the question of whether delaying treatment costs the patient anything.",
        "The adverse events that matter for a surgical population are presented as reassurance. Cholelithiasis occurred in 10% against 3% and hyperglycaemia in 5% against 0%, and the serious treatment-related events in the lanreotide arm include biliary fistula and cholelithiasis, in patients who may later need hepatectomy or arterial therapy; the discussion calls the safety profile favourable by comparison with targeted agents and chemotherapy.",
        "The sponsor controlled the trial end to end. Ipsen, which markets lanreotide, designed, funded and conducted the study; the contract research organisation's statisticians worked under the oversight of the sponsor's own biostatistics department; a medical writer paid by the sponsor drafted the manuscript; and one co-author is affiliated to Ipsen.",
        "Two letters in the New England Journal of Medicine with an author reply are linked to this paper in PubMed (PMIDs 25317882, 25317883 and 25317881). The full texts could not be obtained, so no point above draws on them and whatever objections they raise are not represented here.",
        "Start a somatostatin analogue for antiproliferative effect and symptom control.",
        "Standard",
        "A",
        "Receptor-positive or functional phenotypes, and anyone in whom progression would be hard to salvage. PROMID (n=85, treatment-naive midgut) gave time to progression 14.3 versus 6.0 months, hazard ratio 0.34 (95% CI 0.20–0.59); CLARINET (n=204, non-functioning enteropancreatic, Ki-67 under 10%) gave a progression-free survival hazard ratio of 0.47 (0.30–0.73) with 24-month progression-free survival 65.1% versus 33.0%.",
        "Do not make it mandatory for every patient. Grade A applies to the antiproliferative indication in unresectable disease: PROMID and CLARINET enrolled only patients with no curative option, unresectable disease or declined surgery. In resectable or ablatable disease, analogue versus resection or ablation is an MDT decision.",
        "Neither trial established an overall-survival benefit — CLARINET found no significant difference in overall survival or quality of life, and PROMID is an interim analysis at 67 progressions and 16 deaths of a trial that enrolled 85 of a planned 162 patients and was then closed for slow accrual, so its confirmatory survival analysis at 121 deaths was never performed. The effect is stabilisation, not shrinkage: one partial remission per arm in PROMID, and objective remissions with an analogue are rare. For a liver pathway the decisive limitation is that PROMID's exploratory burden subgroups had imprecise estimates and did not establish a predictive liver-volume threshold — hazard ratio 0.17 (0.08–0.40) at 0 to 10% hepatic involvement, 0.40 (0.10–1.67) at 10 to 50% and 0.71 (0.11–4.45) above 50%, with 95% of patients having Ki-67 of 2% or less and 64/85 (75%) having 10% or less liver involvement, including those without liver disease. CLARINET held across hepatic volume, hazard ratio 0.45 (0.23–0.88) above 25%, but that dichotomy is a post hoc simplification of a prespecified five-category variable whose component hazard ratios ran 0.24 to 0.54. For carcinoid-syndrome control the source is ENETS 2024, not these trials.",
        "Continue the somatostatin analogue for functional-syndrome control where it is needed, and after clinically significant progression in a nonfunctional tumour do not automatically continue it for antiproliferative benefit.",
        "C",
        "Functional disease, where the analogue is doing hormonal work that nothing else in the plan replaces.",
        "Carrying an analogue indefinitely in a nonfunctional tumour that has progressed on it, on the assumption that it is still holding the tumour back.",
        "Downgraded to C: this is a position taken in the absence of evidence rather than from it.         "Do not continue a somatostatin analogue for antiproliferative benefit in every nonfunctional NET after significant progression.",
        "Avoid",
        "B",
        "Continue it for hormonal control where the tumour is functional.",
        "PROMID and CLARINET tested delay of progression in stable, indolent disease — 96% of CLARINET patients had no progression in the 3 to 6 months before randomisation — and neither establishes an antiproliferative role after documented progression.",
        "Octreotide LAR or lanreotide",
        "PROMID: time to progression 14.3 versus 6 months with octreotide versus placebo in midgut NET. CLARINET established PFS benefit with lanreotide in nonfunctional enteropancreatic NET, Ki-67 <10%.",
        "CLARINET randomized double-blind trial, 204 nonfunctioning advanced enteropancreatic NET patients (101 lanreotide, 103 placebo).",
        "From randomization, median PFS not reached with lanreotide versus 18 months placebo; HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.30–0.73). Twenty-four-month PFS 65.1% versus 33.0%. No significant OS or QoL difference in the primary report. Diarrhea 26% versus 9%.",

{
 "slug": "adenoma",
 "prefix": "HCA",
 "questions": [
  {
   "id": "HCA-D1",
   "n": 1,
   "question": "Is MRI with a hepatobiliary contrast agent mandatory before any adenoma is managed as an adenoma, and who may waive it?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "1",
    "6"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "EASL 2016",
     "ref": "27085809",
     "position": "MRI is superior to all other modalities and can subtype up to 80% of adenomas (II-2, grade 1); contrast ultrasound separates adenoma from FNH but cannot subtype.",
     "locator": "Gate 1 · Standard 'Make the diagnosis on contrast-enhanced MRI…' (preferred-for and note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "AFEF 2021 (French multisociety)",
     "ref": "34333196",
     "position": "Adds that a hepatobiliary agent has particular value for identifying focal nodular hyperplasia.",
     "locator": "Gate 1 · Standard 'Make the diagnosis on contrast-enhanced MRI…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "Gaspersz 2019 pregnancy cohort",
     "ref": "31550458",
     "position": "Prospective multicentre cohort: 18 of 66 women (27%) referred with a suspected sub-5 cm adenoma had FNH on hepatobiliary-contrast MRI; the authors held that this misdiagnosis rate justifies the scan, if only to prevent unnecessary anxiety.",
     "locator": "Gate 6 · Standard 'Confirm the diagnosis on MRI with a hepatobiliary contrast agent…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "Haring 2022 resection audit",
     "ref": "36324268",
     "position": "Of 222 Dutch resections for presumed adenoma, 43% had a changed final diagnosis; absence of hepatobiliary MRI independently predicted change (aOR 1.8), an effect the roadmap says is confounded by era and centre.",
     "locator": "Gate 1 · Standard 'Make the diagnosis on contrast-enhanced MRI…' (caveat and note)"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "Sources agree that hepatobiliary-contrast MRI sharpens the adenoma-versus-FNH distinction, but none makes it mandatory or addresses who may waive it, access or cost, and the audit's effect size is confounded.",
   "proposal": "Contrast-enhanced MRI for every patient, with a hepatobiliary agent whenever the question is adenoma versus FNH and always before pregnancy counselling; board triage returns an uncharacterised lesion for imaging rather than discussing it. The roadmap names no one who may waive the requirement.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 1 · Standard 'Make the diagnosis on contrast-enhanced MRI…'; Gate 6 · Standard 'Confirm the diagnosis on MRI with a hepatobiliary contrast agent…'; The board meeting · Triage",
   "rationale": "27% of referred sub-5 cm lesions proved to be focal nodular hyperplasia on hepatobiliary-contrast MRI in the prospective cohort — a lesion needing no follow-up at all. This is an access and cost question as much as a clinical one, so it needs a written answer rather than a preference.",
   "audit": "Audit: proportion characterised before first board discussion, and proportion whose diagnosis changed."
  },
  {
   "id": "HCA-D2",
   "n": 2,
   "question": "Does the programme adopt routine subtyping — a standing four-antibody panel on every specimen and biopsy, with CTNNB1 exon and codon sequencing where activation is suspected, and prostaglandin D synthase for the sonic hedgehog subgroup?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "1",
    "3",
    "10"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "EASL 2016",
     "ref": "27085809",
     "position": "No justification for recommending histopathology or molecular subtyping as routine practice; biopsy may be considered within a benign-tumour MDT to exclude malignancy; imaging-based subtyping needs prospective validation first.",
     "locator": "Gate 1 · Reasonable 'Biopsy when the imaging is atypical…' (caveat); Gate 2 · Reasonable 'Where the subtype is known and low risk…' (caveat)"
    },
    {
     "source": "AISF 2022 (Italian multisociety)",
     "ref": "36089523",
     "position": "Recommends biopsy wherever imaging cannot classify the subtype, specifically to find beta-catenin exon 3 and sonic hedgehog adenomas, but grades this very low quality (D), conditional.",
     "locator": "Gate 1 · Reasonable 'Biopsy when the imaging is atypical…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "ACG 2024",
     "ref": "38958301",
     "position": "Reserves biopsy for cases where imaging is inconclusive (strong recommendation, low-quality evidence).",
     "locator": "Gate 1 · Reasonable 'Biopsy when the imaging is atypical…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "Rebouissou 2016",
     "ref": "27177928",
     "position": "Only 27% of 33 beta-catenin-mutated adenomas showed the strong homogeneous glutamine synthetase pattern and S45 lesions are hard to recognise; the authors call for revised immunohistochemical criteria or mutation screening.",
     "locator": "Gate 1 · Reasonable 'Where tissue exists, ask for the four-antibody panel…' (caveat)"
    },
    {
     "source": "WHO 6th ed., as reviewed (2026)",
     "ref": "42678415",
     "position": "Every inflammatory adenoma should be stained for glutamine synthetase; no reliable routine marker exists for sonic hedgehog adenoma and molecular profiling remains the reference. The roadmap notes it recommends a strategy whose prerequisite it calls unavailable.",
     "locator": "Gate 1 · Standard subtype option 'Sonic hedgehog (shHCA)'; Gate 1 · Reasonable 'Where tissue exists, ask for the four-antibody panel…' (pref); What we are not sure about #9"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "EASL rejects routine subtyping while the Italian guideline, the molecular literature and the local transplant protocol's molecular route presuppose it, and the two subtypes that matter most can be identified reliably only by sequencing.",
   "proposal": "Biopsy is reserved for atypical imaging, suspected transformation or a subtype that would change management. On tissue that exists, the board model makes the four-antibody panel standard and requests CTNNB1 exon and codon where activation is suspected, a transplant route may apply, or the patient is male. Whether to subtype routinely is left to the group.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 1 · Reasonable 'Biopsy when the imaging is atypical…' and 'Where tissue exists, ask for the four-antibody panel…'; Gate 3 · Standard 'Send every male adenoma for expert liver pathology review…'; The board meeting · Pathology; What we are not sure about #8",
   "rationale": "EASL 2016 states there is no justification for recommending routine subtyping. The molecular data since, and the local transplant protocol's own molecular route, both assume it is available. Those two positions cannot both be acted on. [PAYER]",
   "audit": "Registry: subtype assigned, method, concordance with the resection specimen."
  },
  {
   "id": "HCA-D3",
   "n": 3,
   "question": "How long may risk-factor modification run before a persistent lesion over 5 cm is treated — EASL's 6 months, or 12, or longer in a lesion that is still falling?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "2",
    "4"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "EASL 2016",
     "ref": "27085809",
     "position": "Reassess every presumed adenoma with contrast MRI at 6 months; in women, resection is indicated for a nodule still 5 cm or more (II-3, grade 2). EASL also says no robust data define the timeline of stable disease.",
     "locator": "Gate 2 · Standard 'Reimage with contrast-enhanced MRI at 6 months…'; Gate 2 · Reasonable 'Extend observation past 12 months…' (note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "ACG 2024",
     "ref": "38958301",
     "position": "Uses a looser 6- to 12-month imaging interval not tied to a size trigger (conditional, low quality), and holds that lesions of 5 cm or more warrant intervention.",
     "locator": "Gate 2 · Standard 'Reimage with contrast-enhanced MRI at 6 months…'; Gate 4 · Standard 'Treat a lesion that is persistently larger than 5 cm…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "AISF 2022 (Italian multisociety)",
     "ref": "36089523",
     "position": "MRI 6 months after stopping contraception, repeated at 1 year if unchanged or reduced below 5 cm, then annual ultrasound after the first 18 months; every step, including the 6-month decision point, is graded very low quality (D), conditional.",
     "locator": "Gate 2 · Standard 'Reimage with contrast-enhanced MRI at 6 months…'; Gate 4 · Standard (caveat)"
    },
    {
     "source": "Klompenhouwer 2017",
     "ref": "28857134",
     "position": "Of 194 patients with adenomas over 5 cm, 8.5-15.3% had regressed below 5 cm at 26 weeks against 58.5% eventually (median 104 weeks), without complications. The authors propose 12 months for typical non-beta-catenin adenomas in women. 47 of 241 were excluded for short follow-up.",
     "locator": "Gate 2 · Standard 'Reimage with contrast-enhanced MRI at 6 months…' (caveat and note); Gate 2 · Reasonable 'Extend observation past 12 months…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "European practice survey",
     "ref": "36781070",
     "position": "48 of 61 responding experts (79%) advise against routine resection above 5 cm after lifestyle change; the roadmap notes a 21% response rate and stated rather than observed practice.",
     "locator": "Gate 2 · Avoid 'Do not operate on a large adenoma at 6 months…'"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "EASL anchors the decision at 6 months, while ACG uses a looser 6- to 12-month interval. The regression cohort, its authors and most surveyed experts favour waiting longer. The authors' 12-month proposal ignores baseline diameter even though time to regression was strongly size-dependent.",
   "proposal": "Reimage with contrast MRI at 6 months and read it as a trajectory; do not call risk-factor modification a failure before 12 months (grade C, a deliberate deviation from EASL). Observation beyond 12 months is Reasonable in a woman with a typical, non-beta-catenin adenoma that is shrinking. No diameter-specific interval is proposed.",
   "proposal_locator": "What we are not sure about #4; Gate 2 · Standard 'Reimage with contrast-enhanced MRI at 6 months…'; Gate 2 · Reasonable 'Extend observation past 12 months…'",
   "rationale": "EASL and ACG indicate resection at 6 months. At that point only 8.5-15.3% of adenomas over 5 cm have fallen below 5 cm, against 23.7-27.1% at 52 weeks and 58.5% eventually at a median 104 weeks, with no complication during the whole of that follow-up and time to regression strongly size-dependent (median 63 weeks under 7 cm, 208 weeks over 10 cm). The six-month trigger therefore captures roughly one in six to one in ten of the lesions that will eventually regress below 5 cm. The cohort's authors proposed 12 months for typical non-beta-catenin adenomas in women; 79% of responding European experts already decline the rule; and the only GRADE-appraised guideline grades the 6-month decision point very low quality, conditional. Decide the number, and decide whether it differs by baseline diameter.",
   "audit": "Audit: time to fall below 5 cm or to intervention, for every adenoma over 5 cm under surveillance."
  },
  {
   "id": "HCA-D4",
   "n": 4,
   "question": "Does the programme resect every male adenoma irrespective of size, and is expert liver pathology review with sequencing mandatory in every male case?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "3"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "EASL 2016",
     "ref": "27085809",
     "position": "Resection or curative treatment for every adenoma in a man, irrespective of size, because of a higher incidence of malignant transformation (II-3, grade 2).",
     "locator": "Gate 3 · Standard 'Resect, irrespective of size…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "AISF 2022 (Italian multisociety)",
     "ref": "36089523",
     "position": "Also recommends resection in men, as does ACG 2024, but grades it very low quality of evidence (D), conditional.",
     "locator": "Gate 3 · Standard 'Resect, irrespective of size…'; Gate 3 · Reasonable option 'Resection'"
    },
    {

{
 "slug": "hilar",
 "prefix": "pCCA",
 "questions": [
  {
   "id": "pCCA-D1",
   "n": 1,
   "question": "Does the programme open a perihilar transplant protocol, and under whose governance?",
   "kind": "governance",
   "decisions": [
    "4"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "OPTN Policy 9.5.A",
     "ref": "optn",
     "position": "A standardized exception needs a centre holding an OPTN-committee-approved written protocol, neoadjuvant therapy and operative staging; the policy does not prescribe a specific radiotherapy regimen.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · criteria; Gate 4 · Reasonable 'Use the transplant center's approved neoadjuvant treatment protocol…' (note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "12-centre protocol series (Darwish Murad 2012)",
     "ref": "22504095",
     "position": "Intention-to-treat 5-year survival 53% in 287 patients; roadmap critique: retrospective, no arm without neoadjuvant therapy or with resection, 67% from one centre, 25% dropout, selection the only independent predictor of recurrence-free survival.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Reasonable 'Use the transplant center's approved neoadjuvant treatment protocol…' (pref, avoid)"
    },
    {
     "source": "Rea 2005",
     "ref": "16135931",
     "position": "Reported better survival after transplantation than resection; the roadmap says the selection asymmetry is complete, so the paper cannot show transplantation beats resection in a resectable patient.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Avoid 'Do not use Rea 2005 to tell a resectable patient…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "Milan consensus",
     "ref": "40478744",
     "position": "Recommendation 59 supports consideration for selected unresectable or PSC-associated pCCA ≤3.0 cm radial diameter without nodal or distant metastases (strong, level 3), with staging and neoadjuvant therapy specified separately. Recommendation 64 only weakly supports consideration in resectable or questionably resectable disease with appropriate donor access (level 3). Neither establishes universal superiority over resection; the standardized OPTN exception requires a single mass <3 cm in radial diameter.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Avoid 'Do not use Rea 2005…' (note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "AASLD 2023",
     "ref": "36083140",
     "position": "Prefers transplantation over resection in all primary sclerosing cholangitis; the roadmap notes this is expert consensus, not a GRADE-rated guideline, and the 12-centre series found no outcome difference by PSC status.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Standard 'Refer potentially eligible patients to the transplant team…' (note)"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "Milan distinguishes selected unresectable/PSC-associated disease from a weaker recommendation for resectable or questionably resectable disease; AASLD has its own PSC preference. Supporting transplant comparisons are retrospective and heavily selected, and TRANSPHIL failed to recruit. Opening a protocol remains an institutional decision under the applicable OPTN requirements.",
   "proposal": "The roadmap does not say whether to open the protocol. It classes neoadjuvant therapy plus transplantation as Reasonable (grade C, PROTOCOL, REGISTRY) only at a centre holding an OPTN-approved written protocol, routes potentially eligible patients to early transplant review, treats graft stewardship as institutional judgement, and requires a registry if the pathway opens.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 4 · Standard 'Refer potentially eligible patients…' and Reasonable 'Use the transplant center's approved neoadjuvant treatment protocol…'; What we are not sure about · item 9; Decisions · item 1 (audit)",
   "rationale": "Supporting data are retrospective multicentre protocol experience with heavy selection. Graft stewardship is an institutional judgement.",
   "audit": "Registry required if opened."
  },

   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [

   ],
   "positions": [
    {

   ],

   "proposal": "No default is set. Bland embolisation and conventional TACE are both Reasonable (grade C), chosen by burden, symptoms, liver reserve and biliary-infection risk and not treated as interchangeable; drug-eluting embolics are avoided.    "rationale": "RETNET reported randomized TAE-versus-cTACE results at NANETS 2025 without a significant hepatic-PFS difference; this does not establish equivalence. Its drug-eluting-bead arm had closed after an early safety signal. One small randomised TAE versus TACE trial (Maire 2012, 26 patients, cited from ENETS rather than read in full) found no significant 2-year progression-free survival difference but was underpowered. The best non-randomised comparison favours bland embolisation on response in carcinoid disease (81.0% versus 44.4%, odds ratio 6.41) with no survival difference, but treatment was chosen by the referring physician; ENETS 2024 prefers bland in small-intestine NET while ENETS 2023 calls chemoembolisation possibly more effective in functioning pancreatic NET. {
 "slug": "pcyst",
 "prefix": "PCYST",
 "questions": [
  {
   "id": "PCYST-D1",
   "n": 1,
   "question": "Which guideline is this programme's spine — Kyoto 2024, ACG 2018, the European 2018 guideline, or AGA 2015?",
   "kind": "governance",
   "decisions": [],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v1.2026",
     "ref": "nccn",
     "position": "Offers no cyst algorithm of its own; summarises the international and European groups, names Kyoto 2024 the international standard, cites the superseded 2013 European statement, and tells readers to use the most recent available guideline.",
     "locator": "Quick reference 'Resection thresholds compared, and the non-IPMN cysts' · row 'NCCN v1.2026'; Provenance"
    },
    {
     "source": "Kyoto 2024",
     "ref": "38182527",
     "position": "The most recent guideline and the only one built on systematic reviews commissioned question by question; its own authors concede most IPMN studies lack high-level evidence, and it covers IPMN only, with no intervals for other cysts.",
     "locator": "Practice choices with limited evidence · item 1; Gate 8 · Standard option 'Kyoto 2024 schedule'"
    },
    {
     "source": "ACG 2018",
     "ref": "29485131",
     "position": "The size-stratified schedule most US radiologists recognise, with MRCP preferred; graded conditional on very low quality evidence by ACG itself, which also says there are very few data on extending intervals and none on stopping by age.",
     "locator": "Gate 8 · Standard option 'ACG 2018 schedule'"
    },
    {
     "source": "European 2018",
     "ref": "29574408",
     "position": "The simplest schedule to run and audit, since it does not branch on size, and the only one that also covers non-IPMN cysts; but the most imaging-intensive for a small stable cyst, with no demonstrated outcome advantage.",
     "locator": "Gate 8 · Standard option 'European 2018 schedule'"
    },
    {
     "source": "AGA 2015",
     "ref": "25805375",
     "position": "The least intensive schedule and the only one with an explicit endpoint, but every recommendation is conditional on very low quality evidence and the AGA says its own surveillance interval has no evidence behind it.",
     "locator": "Gate 8 · Standard option 'AGA 2015 schedule'; Practice choices with limited evidence · item 28"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "The four guidelines disagree on intervals, resection thresholds and stopping, NCCN declines to choose among them, and no study compares management under any of them on any outcome.",
   "proposal": "The roadmap uses Kyoto 2024 as its provisional spine (most recent, built on commissioned systematic reviews, cited by NCCN) while stating this is a choice, not demonstrated superiority. It takes non-IPMN management from the European guideline and ACG, and shows what the other three guidelines would do instead.",
   "proposal_locator": "Practice choices with limited evidence · item 1; Gate 5 · Reasonable 'Where the entity cannot be settled on imaging…' note; Provenance",
   "rationale": "NCCN takes no position and tells the reader to use the most recent available cyst guideline. The four differ on intervals, on resection thresholds and on stopping, and no study compares them. Until one is named, the same patient is managed differently depending on who sees them.",
   "audit": "Guideline and version recorded on every board output; proportion of cases managed off the named schedule."
  },
  {
   "id": "PCYST-D2",
   "n": 2,
   "question": "Which surveillance interval schedule, stated by size band, and which modality?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "8"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "Kyoto 2024",
     "ref": "38182527",
     "position": "Under 20 mm: 6 months, then 18-monthly if stable; 20 to under 30 mm: 6 months twice, then yearly; 30 mm or more: 6-monthly; CT or MRI. Alone in having progression data under its bands, but IPMN only.",
     "locator": "Gate 8 · Standard option 'Kyoto 2024 schedule'"
    },
    {
     "source": "ACG 2018",
     "ref": "29485131",
     "position": "Escalates with size, from MRI every 2 years under 1 cm to MRI alternating with EUS 6-monthly over 3 cm, with lengthening once stability is shown; MRCP preferred. Conditional recommendation on very low quality evidence.",
     "locator": "Gate 8 · Standard option 'ACG 2018 schedule'; Gate 8 · Standard 'Use MRI with MRCP…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "European 2018",
     "ref": "29574408",
     "position": "MRI preferred; 6-monthly in the first year, then yearly for life while fit for surgery, regardless of size and for MCN under 40 mm alike; 6-monthly for relative indications, elderly and comorbid patients. Most imaging-intensive for small stable cysts.",
     "locator": "Gate 8 · Standard option 'European 2018 schedule'"
    },
    {
     "source": "AGA 2015",
     "ref": "25805375",
     "position": "For cysts under 3 cm without a solid component or dilated duct: MRI at 1 year, then every 2 years, stopping at 5 years. The AGA says the interval is not based on evidence.",
     "locator": "Gate 8 · Standard option 'AGA 2015 schedule'"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "The schedules differ threefold or more in imaging per patient-decade for the same cyst, have never been compared on any outcome, and three of the four concede their intervals lack an evidence base.",
   "proposal": "Choose one schedule, adopt it whole without mixing intervals and stopping rules from different guidelines, and record its name and version. The page's spine is the Kyoto 2024 schedule, with non-IPMN intervals still to be borrowed. Image with MRI and MRCP wherever available, CT only where MRI is unsuitable, keeping one modality throughout.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 8 · Standard options local approval note and option 'Kyoto 2024 schedule'; Gate 8 · Standard 'Use MRI with MRCP…'; Gate 8 · Avoid 'Do not mix the four schedules…'; Gate 1 · Reasonable 'Pancreas-protocol CT is an acceptable substitute…'",
   "rationale": "The four schedules differ by a factor of three or more in imaging per patient-decade for the same cyst, and three of the four state in their own texts that their intervals are not evidence-based. A schedule assembled case by case cannot be audited and cannot generate a growth rate. The ACG 2 to 3 cm band is now resolved from the full text — MRI or EUS every 6 to 12 months for 3 years, then yearly for 4 — so the remaining question is which guideline, not which reading of a figure.",
   "audit": "Schedule assigned at enrolment; adherence to interval; proportion of scans on the assigned modality."
  },
  {
   "id": "PCYST-D3",
   "n": 3,
   "question": "The stopping rule: continue while fit, stop at 5 years of stability, or stop by age and size?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "9"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "European 2018",
     "ref": "29574408",
     "position": "Follows patients without a surgical indication until they are no longer fit for surgery (GRADE 1B), reasoning that the risk of IPMN progression rises over time.",
     "locator": "Gate 9 · Standard option 'Continue while the patient remains fit — European 2018 and ACG 2018'"
    },
    {
     "source": "ACG 2018",
     "ref": "29485131",
     "position": "Stops only on loss of surgical candidacy, reassesses utility over 75 and individualises at 76 to 85 (age limits it admits are borrowed and unsupported), and rejects the AGA 5-year rule, citing a 15 to 20-year dwell time.",
     "locator": "Gate 9 · Standard option 'Continue while the patient remains fit…'; Gate 9 · Standard 'Stop when the patient is no longer a candidate…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "AGA 2015",
     "ref": "25805375",
     "position": "Stop after 5 years without significant change (conditional, very low quality); not restricted by size, and resting on a population-level transformation estimate with no data comparing stable and changing cysts, which the guideline admits.",
     "locator": "Gate 9 · Standard option 'Stop at 5 years if stable — AGA 2015, and one of Kyoto 2024's two options'"
    },
    {
     "source": "Kyoto 2024",
     "ref": "38182527",
     "position": "Offers two options for a small unchanged branch-duct IPMN at 5 years: stop if under 20 mm without worrisome features, weighing life expectancy, or continue for concomitant adenocarcinoma; not for younger or familial-risk patients.",
     "locator": "Gate 9 · Standard option 'Stop at 5 years if stable…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "Marchegiani 2023",
     "ref": "37406887",
     "position": "After 5 years of stability, standardised incidence ratios of 1.12 at 75 or over and 0.95 at 65 or over with cysts of 15 mm or less underpin the authors' proposal to stop at over 75 with cysts under 30 mm, or at 65 or over with cysts of 15 mm or less; the roadmap notes these rest on 3 and 2 cancers.",
     "locator": "Gate 9 · Standard option 'Stop by age and size — the standardised-incidence-ratio argument'; Practice choices with limited evidence · item 16"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "The three cohorts behind these positions reach opposite conclusions, which the roadmap attributes to differences in baseline selection, conditioning on 5-year survival, counting high-grade dysplasia as an event and length of follow-up, and no study has randomised stopping.",
   "proposal": "No winner is picked. The roadmap applies only the shared rule (stop when the patient is no longer a surgical candidate, judged on fitness not age and reassessed each visit) and holds that competing risk, not incidence ratios, is the sound argument for stopping. Any stop is a recorded decision explained to the patient, never a lapsed recall.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 9 · Standard 'Stop when the patient is no longer a candidate…'; Gate 9 · Standard options order note; Practice choices with limited evidence · item 15; Gate 9 · Avoid 'Do not call stopping a discharge…' and 'Do not let surveillance stop by default…'",
   "rationale": "Each has a different failure mode. Continuing indefinitely commits imaging to patients who will die of something else; stopping at 5 years accepts a documented 4.4% rate of invasive cancer after that point in one referral cohort; the age-and-size rule rests on two and three cancers with confidence intervals compatible with a threefold excess, in a retrospective cohort no guideline has endorsed. The three supporting cohorts differ in baseline selection, in conditioning on survival to 5 years, in whether high-grade dysplasia counts as an event against an invasive-cancer comparator, and in how long they watched past the mark — and those four differences account for their opposite conclusions. Choosing a rule means choosing one of those designs.",
   "audit": "Stopping decisions by rule applied, and any pancreatic cancer diagnosed after surveillance stopped, reported as a named event."
  },
  {
   "id": "PCYST-D4",
   "n": 4,
   "question": "Does a cyst of 30 mm, or 40 mm, trigger resection on size alone in a fit patient?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "2",
    "3"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "Sendai 2006",
     "ref": "16327281",
     "position": "Made a branch-duct cyst over 30 mm a resection trigger, on multivariate analyses in two series of 15 and 32 patients, while saying more pathological data were needed before resecting all such lesions.",
     "locator": "Gate 2 · Avoid 'Do not treat a cyst of 30 mm or more as a high-risk stigma…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "Fukuoka 2017",
     "ref": "28735806",
     "position": "Holds that size by itself, being a poor predictor, should not indicate surgery, but retains 3 cm as a worrisome feature and lets 2 cm count in patients younger than 65.",
     "locator": "Gate 2 · Avoid 'Do not treat a cyst of 30 mm or more as a high-risk stigma…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "Kyoto 2024",
     "ref": "38182527",
     "position": "Keeps a cyst of 30 mm or more as a worrisome feature rather than a high-risk stigma, and treats multiple worrisome features as additive.",
     "locator": "Gate 2 · Avoid 'Do not treat a cyst of 30 mm or more…'; Gate 3 · Standard 'Count the worrisome features…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "European 2018",
     "ref": "29574408",
     "position": "Makes a cyst of 40 mm or more a relative indication for surgery, without a head-to-head comparison, while its own text gives a 27 to 33% positive predictive value for a 30 mm cyst lacking other risk factors.",
     "locator": "Gate 2 · Avoid 'Do not treat a cyst of 30 mm or more…' note"
    },
    {
     "source": "Revised Kyoto validation",
     "ref": "38880125",
     "position": "A single worrisome feature carried a non-significant hazard of later cancer (SHR 1.43, 0.93 to 2.19), and risk was stratified at 20 mm but not at 30 mm.",
     "locator": "Gate 2 · Avoid 'Do not treat a cyst of 30 mm or more…' note; Gate 3 · Avoid 'Do not read one worrisome feature as an indication to operate'"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "Sendai and the European guideline treat size as grounds to operate (30 and 40 mm), the IAP guidelines since 2012 do not, and the only large validation found that 30 mm did not stratify risk.",
   "proposal": "Not on size alone. The roadmap counts a cyst of 30 mm or more as one worrisome feature, lets the count, trajectory and fitness drive the next step, and advises against operating on a single worrisome feature, while acknowledging that the European 40 mm relative indication remains a live position held by serious people.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 2 · Avoid 'Do not treat a cyst of 30 mm or more as a high-risk stigma…'; Gate 3 · Avoid 'Do not read one worrisome feature as an indication to operate'; Decisions table · item 4 · why",
   "rationale": "Sendai 2006 made more than 30 mm a resection trigger from multivariate analyses in two series of 15 and 32 patients; Fukuoka 2012 demoted size on the ground that it is a weaker indicator than nodules or cytology; Fukuoka 2017 said size alone is not an appropriate parameter to indicate surgery while keeping 3 cm as a worrisome feature and 2 cm as a consideration under 65; Kyoto 2024 keeps it as a worrisome feature; the European guideline makes 40 mm a relative indication. A single worrisome feature carried a non-significant hazard ratio in the validation cohort, and that same cohort found risk stratified at 20 mm but not at 30 mm. The evidence does not support size alone — but the European position is live and is held by serious people.",
   "audit": "Resections by largest cyst dimension and by number of worrisome features, with final histology."
  },
  {
   "id": "PCYST-D5",
   "n": 5,
   "question": "Mucinous cystic neoplasm: resect all in fit patients, or surveil those under 40 mm without risk features?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "5"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v1.2026",
     "ref": "nccn",
     "position": "Summarising the international group, recommends resecting all MCNs in patients who can undergo surgery, and puts the malignant risk below 15%.",
     "locator": "Gate 5 · Standard option 'Mucinous cystic neoplasm — resect, but where is the threshold?'"

     "locator": "Gate 5 · Standard option 'Mucinous cystic neoplasm — resect, but where is the threshold?'"

     "ref": "16327281",
     "position": "Originated 'resect all' on 6 to 36% malignancy rates from series that mostly did not require ovarian-type stroma, which its own text concedes inflates them, and on an asserted low risk of distal pancreatectomy.",
     "locator": "Gate 5 · Standard option 'Mucinous cystic neoplasm…' caveat"

    {
     "source": "Fukuoka 2012",
     "ref": "22687371",
     "position": "Reported under 15% invasive carcinoma in series requiring ovarian-type stroma, and no malignancy below 4 cm without mural nodules; its resect-all position stayed in force unexamined after Fukuoka 2017 dropped MCN from scope.",
     "locator": "Gate 5 · Standard option 'Mucinous cystic neoplasm…'; Gate 5 · Standard options local approval note"

    {
     "source": "ACG 2018",
     "ref": "29485131",
     "position": "Found high-grade dysplasia or cancer in 10% of 90 resected MCNs, with none under 3 cm that had a normal CA 19-9 and no concerning features.",
     "locator": "Gate 5 · Standard option 'Mucinous cystic neoplasm…'"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "NCCN's summary of the international group says resect all while the European guideline says surveil under 40 mm without risk features; Kyoto 2024 does not adjudicate, and the roadmap calls this the sharpest disagreement on the page.",
   "proposal": "The roadmap does not choose, but reports that its full-text read moves the balance toward the European position (surveil presumed MCN under 40 mm without risk features; resect at 40 mm, or with symptoms or a nodule), conceding that 'resect all' is held by serious people because invasion is hard to detect preoperatively. Age-dependent thresholds remain open.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 5 · Standard options local approval note; Gate 5 · Standard option 'Mucinous cystic neoplasm — resect, but where is the threshold?'",
   "rationale": "NCCN, summarising the international group, says resect all; the European evidence-based guideline says it is safe to follow those under 40 mm. The malignant risk is under 15%, and the two positions differ by a substantial number of distal pancreatectomies a year.",
   "audit": "Mucinous cystic neoplasms by size, management chosen, and final histology in every resected case."
  },
  {
   "id": "PCYST-D6",
   "n": 6,
   "question": "Cyst fluid panel: does glucose replace CEA as first-line, is cytology mandatory on every aspirate, and is molecular testing offered and funded?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "4"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "Glucose meta-analysis",
     "ref": "33964311",
     "position": "Head to head, glucose sensitivity was 91% against CEA's 56% and accuracy 94% against 85%; adding CEA did not improve on glucose. The roadmap notes both glucose meta-analyses pool largely the same seven studies.",

     "position": "Quotes glucose under 50 mg/dL (93% sensitivity, 89% specificity) without recommending it, makes suspicious cytology a high-risk stigma, and gives its molecular recommendations its highest evidence level (1+, grade B).",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Standard options 'Cyst fluid glucose', 'Cytology' and 'Targeted next-generation sequencing of cyst fluid'; Gate 4 local approval note"

    {

     "ref": "29485131",
     "position": "Says cytology should be sent to assess for high-grade dysplasia, does not name glucose, and judges molecular markers early in development with insufficient evidence for routine use.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Standard options 'Cytology' and 'Targeted next-generation sequencing of cyst fluid'; Gate 4 local approval note"

     "ref": "29574408",
     "position": "Does not name glucose; KRAS and GNAS testing may be considered (GRADE 2C) only when the diagnosis is unclear and the result would change management.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Standard option 'Targeted next-generation sequencing of cyst fluid'; Gate 4 local approval note"

   "rationale": "Glucose outperformed CEA head to head on pooled data, but neither ACG nor the European guideline names it, Kyoto quotes it without recommending it, and the two meta-analyses behind it pool largely the same seven primary studies so are not independent confirmation of each other. [PAYER]",

{
 "slug": "pdac",
 "prefix": "PDAC",
 "questions": [
  {
   "id": "PDAC-D1",
   "n": 1,
   "question": "For an anatomically resectable tumour with no high-risk features, is the local default upfront resection with adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX, or a neoadjuvant route — and if neoadjuvant, which regimen?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "3"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (extracted text, 22 Apr 2026)",
     "ref": "nccn",
     "position": "Upfront surgery then postoperative therapy has been the standard; neoadjuvant therapy is permitted in resectable disease, especially with high-risk features, but evidence for specific regimens off-trial is limited. Either PREOPANC-2 regimen may be considered.",
     "locator": "Gate 3 · Standard group · options 'Upfront resection, then adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX' and 'Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX, then surgery' (when); Reasonable 'Neoadjuvant chemotherapy for a resectable tumour that has high-risk features…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "ESMO 2023 pancreatic guideline",
     "ref": "37678671",
     "position": "Recommends against neoadjuvant therapy for resectable disease outside clinical trials, citing limited phase III evidence [II, E]. The roadmap notes it predates PREOPANC-2, NORPACT-1 and the 2025 meta-analyses and describes no search strategy.",
     "locator": "Gate 3 · Standard group · option 'Upfront resection, then adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX' (when); What we are not sure about · 'ESMO's 2023 guideline recommends against neoadjuvant therapy…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "NORPACT-1",
     "ref": "38237621",
     "position": "The only randomised trial of neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX against upfront surgery restricted to resectable head cancer; its primary endpoint favoured upfront surgery (18-month survival 73% vs 60%). The roadmap reads it as no benefit shown: phase 2 at alpha 0.15, non-significant per protocol, and 21% of the neoadjuvant arm never received FOLFIRINOX and went straight to resection.",
     "locator": "Gate 3 · Standard group · option 'Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX, then surgery' (avoid, note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "PREOPANC long-term",
     "ref": "35084987",
     "position": "Neoadjuvant gemcitabine chemoradiotherapy improved long-term survival (HR 0.73) in mixed resectable and borderline disease after a negative primary analysis; resectable subgroup non-significant (HR 0.79), and half the control arm received no chemotherapy.",
     "locator": "Gate 3 · Standard group · option 'Neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy, then surgery, then adjuvant gemcitabine' (when, avoid, note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "PREOPANC-2",
     "ref": "40945523",
     "position": "Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX without adjuvant therapy and the PREOPANC chemoradiotherapy regimen gave similar survival (21.9 vs 21.3 months, HR 0.88), with no upfront-surgery arm; the roadmap calls it a failed superiority trial that justifies FOLFIRINOX if neoadjuvant.",
     "locator": "Gate 3 · Standard group · option 'Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX, then surgery' (when, pref)"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "NCCN permits and ESMO advises against neoadjuvant therapy in resectable disease; NORPACT-1 pointed to upfront surgery and PREOPANC to neoadjuvant treatment in a mixed population, the pooled resectable subgroup shows no benefit (HR 0.90), and no trial has tested the comparator with adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX.",
   "proposal": "The roadmap lists upfront resection then adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX first for fit patients without high-risk features, as what randomised evidence supports, while saying it does not resolve the question. If a neoadjuvant route is chosen - for named high-risk features, or where the board judges selecting out occult metastatic disease worth the resection-rate cost - tissue comes first and the regimen is FOLFIRINOX, or PREOPANC chemoradiotherapy if FOLFIRINOX is not tolerable; offer a randomised trial where one is recruiting (A021806 is active but not recruiting).",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 3 · Standard group (order note, flagnote and options); Reasonable 'Neoadjuvant chemotherapy for a resectable tumour that has high-risk features…'; Avoid 'Do not start neoadjuvant therapy without a tissue diagnosis.'",
   "rationale": "The trials disagree and the page does not resolve them, and the full-text read made the disagreement worse rather than better. No neoadjuvant trial gave its control arm modern adjuvant therapy except NORPACT-1, and there only 19 of 44 resected control patients (43%) received adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX; PREOPANC's control arm received adjuvant gemcitabine and only 51% of it received any chemotherapy; PREOPANC-2 has no upfront-surgery arm; S1505 and A021501 had no randomised control at all. Pooled across nine randomised trials the resectable subgroup shows no benefit (HR 0.90, 0.63–1.28) and the borderline resectable subgroup does (HR 0.60, 0.38–0.96), but the between-subgroup test is not significant (p=0.081) and the pooled estimate depends on post hoc removal of NORPACT-1. NORPACT-1's primary endpoint favoured upfront surgery at a two-sided alpha of 0.15, was non-significant per protocol, and had 21% of its neoadjuvant arm go straight to resection without the drug. ESMO recommends against neoadjuvant therapy in resectable disease at [II, E]. The pooled data also show no gain in adjuvant initiation (57.7% versus 55.6%, p=0.353), which removes the main mechanistic argument. A021806 has not reported. This has to be a local decision because there is no guideline answer to copy and no trial of the comparison that matters.",
   "audit": "Registry: resectability category, sequence chosen, resection rate, R0 rate, time from diagnosis to first treatment, and proportion of resected patients who never start adjuvant therapy."
  },
  {
   "id": "PDAC-D2",
   "n": 2,
   "question": "Does this programme offer arterial resection, or arterial divestment, for PDAC — and if so at what minimum volume, by which surgeons, and under what consent document?",
   "kind": "governance",
   "decisions": [
    "4",
    "7"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (extracted text, 22 Apr 2026)",
     "ref": "nccn",
     "position": "Restricts arterial resection to centres with proven vascular-reconstruction experience and highly selected patients with objective response after extensive neoadjuvant therapy, with counselling that long-term benefit is unknown; it names no volume threshold anywhere.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Reasonable group · option 'Arterial resection (hepatic artery, celiac axis, SMA)' (when, pref); Gate 5 · Reasonable 'A written minimum annual volume for pancreatoduodenectomy…' (pref, note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "PRODIGE 24 five-year",
     "ref": "36048453",
     "position": "A post hoc model linked centres enrolling 10 or more patients to better survival (HR 0.77); the roadmap calls it stepwise-selected, uncorrected for multiplicity and confounded, not a derived volume threshold.",
     "locator": "Gate 5 · Reasonable 'A written minimum annual volume for pancreatoduodenectomy…' (note); What we are not sure about · 'Whether to offer arterial resection or arterial divestment…'"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "No source sets a volume, surgeon or consent standard; NCCN restricts the operation only qualitatively and the one volume signal is a confounded post hoc association.",
   "proposal": "Undecided. The roadmap treats arterial resection as a highly selected salvage ('almost nobody'), considered only after a significant response and never for a minimal one, with NCCN's counselling that the chance of cure is unknown. It proposes a written minimum annual pancreatoduodenectomy volume with outcome audit but states no number.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 4 · Reasonable group · option 'Arterial resection…' and Avoid 'Do not operate for a minimal response when the operation required is an arterial resection.'; Gate 5 · Reasonable 'A written minimum annual volume…'; What we are not sure about · 'Whether to offer arterial resection or arterial divestment…'",
   "rationale": "NCCN restricts it to centres with proven experience in pancreatectomy with vascular resection and reconstruction, in highly selected patients after extensive neoadjuvant therapy with objective response, and requires patients to be told that the long-term benefit is currently unknown. It names no threshold. This is a governance decision taken once, not a decision taken in the room.",
   "audit": "Audit: volume, 90-day mortality and R0 rate by vascular resection type; consent document on file."
  },
  {
   "id": "PDAC-D3",
   "n": 3,
   "question": "What counts locally as a significant response after neoadjuvant therapy, and who decides?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "4",
    "7"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (extracted text, 22 Apr 2026)",
     "ref": "nccn",
     "position": "Leaves the degree of significance to the local team, offering examples: CA 19-9 normalisation, near-normalisation or at least 50% fall, and complete or near-complete PET response; judge on two of three metrics, riskier operations needing bigger responses.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Standard 'Restage … and judge response on two of three metrics' (pref, note); Gate 4 · Reasonable group (avoid of option 'Arterial resection…')"
    },
    {
     "source": "ESMO 2023 pancreatic guideline",
     "ref": "37678671",
     "position": "Cites a pooled analysis (17 studies, 2,242 patients) linking a CA 19-9 fall over 50% or normalisation to better survival; warns imaging performs worse after chemotherapy and persistent perivascular soft tissue is not necessarily residual tumour.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Standard 'Restage … and judge response on two of three metrics' (pref, avoid, note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "NORPACT-1",
     "ref": "38237621",
     "position": "Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX improved R0 (56% vs 39%) and N0 (29% vs 14%) while survival went the other way; the roadmap uses this, with PREOPANC-2 and ESPAC5, to argue pathologic surrogates do not track survival.",
     "locator": "What we are not sure about · 'What counts as a significant response after neoadjuvant therapy…'"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "NCCN supplies examples but delegates the threshold, ESMO supports CA 19-9 as the best-evidenced metric, and trial data show pathologic response moving without survival, so no source defines significance.",
   "proposal": "No definition proposed; the roadmap makes it a local approval item. Interim rule: judge response on at least two of three metrics (radiologic, CA 19-9 or CEA, PET), add a third and discuss at the board when they conflict, still explore without shrinkage if there is no extrapancreatic progression, and require a significant response before arterial resection.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 4 · Standard 'Restage … and judge response on two of three metrics' (pref, note); Gate 1 · Avoid 'Do not re-stage off a post-neoadjuvant scan alone…'; Gate 4 · Avoid 'Do not operate for a minimal response when the operation required is an arterial resection.'",
   "rationale": "NCCN hands the definition to the local treatment team and offers only examples — CA 19-9 normalisation, near-normalisation or at least a 50% decrease, and a complete or near-complete metabolic response on PET. Since the response category determines whether a vascular resection is offered, an unwritten definition is applied inconsistently.",
   "audit": "Audit: response category recorded for every neoadjuvant patient, resection attempted, R0 rate."
  },
  {
   "id": "PDAC-D4",
   "n": 4,
   "question": "Is mFOLFIRINOX the adjuvant default for every recovered good-performance-status patient, and what threshold moves a patient to gemcitabine with capecitabine?",
   "kind": "clinical",
   "decisions": [
    "6"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (extracted text, 22 Apr 2026)",
     "ref": "nccn",
     "position": "Lists mFOLFIRINOX and gemcitabine with capecitabine as preferred adjuvant options for patients who had no neoadjuvant therapy, and gemcitabine alone as an other recommended option.",
     "locator": "Gate 6 · Standard group · options 'mFOLFIRINOX for 24 weeks', 'Gemcitabine with capecitabine' and 'Gemcitabine alone' (when)"
    },
    {
     "source": "ESMO 2023 pancreatic guideline",
     "ref": "37678671",
     "position": "mFOLFIRINOX for fit patients [I, A]; gemcitabine with capecitabine as the alternative for patients over 75, ECOG 2 or with a contraindication to mFOLFIRINOX [I, B]; complete 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy [I, A].",
     "locator": "Gate 6 · Standard group · options 'mFOLFIRINOX for 24 weeks' and 'Gemcitabine with capecitabine' (when)"
    },
    {
     "source": "PRODIGE 24 five-year",

    {
     "source": "ENETS 2023 NF-PanNET",
     "ref": "37877341",
     "position": "Read in full: active surveillance at 1 cm or less without duct dilation; above 1 cm to 2 cm personalised to the resection required and comorbidity with no rule; surgery strongly recommended above 2 cm (level 3, grade B).",

     "locator": "Gate 4 · Standard 'State the actual evidence for the threshold…' · note"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "The guidelines agree at 1 cm but every source hands the 1–2 cm band back to the clinician, and the only systematic comparison found no difference at low certainty, so any default is a judgement rather than a finding.",

def item(text, *refs): return dict(text=text, refs=list(refs))
def nested(text, children, *refs): return dict(text=text, refs=list(refs), children=children)
def group(label, *items): return dict(label=label, items=list(items))
def branch(title, criteria, action, to=None, kind='advance', refs=()):
    return dict(title=title, criteria=criteria, action=action, to=to, kind=kind, refs=list(refs))
def step(id, title, question, owner, timing, orders, branches, stops=(), issues=()):
    return dict(id=id,title=title,question=question,owner=owner,timing=timing,orders=orders,branches=branches,stops=list(stops),issues=list(issues))
def comparison(ref, text, quote=False, locator=''):
    return dict(ref=ref,text=text,quote=quote,locator=locator)
def issue(id, question, comparisons, proposal, rationale, owners, record):
    return dict(id=id,question=question,comparisons=comparisons,proposal=proposal,rationale=rationale,owners=owners,record=record,status='Discussion required — not yet approved')
def pathway(slug,code,name,route,entry,roadmap,steps,issues):
    files=json.loads((ROOT.parent/'assets/documents.json').read_text())['tumors'][slug]['files']
    base=f'/mh-liver-pathways/documents/{slug}/'
    return dict(slug=slug,code=code,name=name,route=route,entry=entry,roadmap=roadmap,
                steps=steps,issues=issues,protocol=base+files['standard_info'],
                docs=[dict(label=label,url=base+files[slot]) for slot,label in [('decision','Decision discussion'),('standard_questions','Standard pathway questions')]])

Clinical content is a review draft, not an automated eligibility determination.
References are attached to individual claims; local choices remain labelled draft.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import json

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DIST = ROOT / 'dist'
POLICY = 'https://www.hrsa.gov/sites/default/files/hrsa/optn/optn_policies.pdf'
GUIDANCE = 'https://www.hrsa.gov/sites/default/files/hrsa/optn/adult-meld-exception-transplant-oncology-review-guidance.pdf'

def source(short, title, kind, locator, url, pattern=None, page=None, note=''):
    matches = sorted((DIST / 'evidence').rglob(pattern)) if pattern else []
    return dict(short=short, title=title, kind=kind, locator=locator, url=url,
                pdf=('/' + matches[0].relative_to(DIST).as_posix() + (f'#page={page}' if page else '')) if matches else url,
                note=note)

def item(text, *refs): return dict(text=text, refs=list(refs))
def nested(text, children, *refs): return dict(text=text, refs=list(refs), children=children)
def group(label, *items): return dict(label=label, items=list(items))
def branch(title, criteria, action, to=None, kind='advance', refs=()):
    return dict(title=title, criteria=criteria, action=action, to=to, kind=kind, refs=list(refs))
def step(id, title, question, owner, timing, orders, branches, stops=(), issues=()):
    return dict(id=id,title=title,question=question,owner=owner,timing=timing,orders=orders,branches=branches,stops=list(stops),issues=list(issues))
def comparison(ref, text, quote=False, locator=''):
    return dict(ref=ref,text=text,quote=quote,locator=locator)
def issue(id, question, comparisons, proposal, rationale, owners, record):
    return dict(id=id,question=question,comparisons=comparisons,proposal=proposal,rationale=rationale,owners=owners,record=record,status='Discussion required — not yet approved')
def pathway(slug,code,name,route,entry,roadmap,steps,issues):
    files=json.loads((ROOT.parent/'assets/documents.json').read_text())['tumors'][slug]['files']
    base=f'/mh-liver-pathways/documents/{slug}/'
    return dict(slug=slug,code=code,name=name,route=route,entry=entry,roadmap=roadmap,
                steps=steps,issues=issues,protocol=base+files['standard_info'],
                docs=[dict(label=label,url=base+files[slot]) for slot,label in [('decision','Decision discussion'),('standard_questions','Standard pathway questions')]])

def option(value, label, *details):
    return dict(value=value, label=label, details=list(details))

def question(id, label, options, refs, help='', criteria=()):
    return dict(id=id, label=label, options=options+[option('unknown','Uncertain / not yet assessed')],
                refs=list(refs), help=help, criteria=list(criteria))

def criterion(title, items, refs, show_for=()):
    return dict(title=title, items=items, refs=list(refs), show_for=list(show_for))

def rule(when, branch=None, kind=None, title=None, text=None, refs=()):
    return dict(when=when, branch=branch, kind=kind, title=title, text=text, refs=list(refs))

def pause(when, title, text, refs):
    return rule(when, kind='hold', title=title, text=text, refs=refs)

def stop(when, text, refs, title='Review the treatment and transplant plan'):
    return rule(when, kind='stop', title=title, text=text, refs=refs)

def yesno(id, label, refs, help='', yes='Yes', no='No'):
    return question(id,label,[option('yes',yes),option('no',no)],refs,help)

"""Essential, source-linked choices for the 46 existing transplant decisions.

These rules select a passage to review, not a transplant eligibility verdict.
Stop/clarification rules precede proceed rules. Every proceed rule specifies all
questions in that decision. No identifiers, raw clinical records or dates.
"""
VERSION = '2026-10-24.6'

def option(value, label, *details):
    return dict(value=value, label=label, details=list(details))

def question(id, label, options, refs, help='', criteria=()):
    return dict(id=id, label=label, options=options+[option('unknown','Uncertain / not yet assessed')],
                refs=list(refs), help=help, criteria=list(criteria))

def criterion(title, items, refs, show_for=()):
    return dict(title=title, items=items, refs=list(refs), show_for=list(show_for))

def rule(when, branch=None, kind=None, title=None, text=None, refs=()):
    return dict(when=when, branch=branch, kind=kind, title=title, text=text, refs=list(refs))

def pause(when, title, text, refs):
    return rule(when, kind='hold', title=title, text=text, refs=refs)

def stop(when, text, refs, title='Review the treatment and transplant plan'):
    return rule(when, kind='stop', title=title, text=text, refs=refs)

def yesno(id, label, refs, help='', yes='Yes', no='No'):
    return question(id,label,[option('yes',yes),option('no',no)],refs,help)

    ASSISTANTS[f'{pathway}/{step}']=dict(questions=questions,rules=rules)

[
 "Name the accountable system HCC pathway owner and the neutral tumour-board chair.",
 "Approve the Epic submission form, the MDT note template, the registry minimum dataset and the urgent-case rule.",
 "Approve modality-specific liver-function and dosimetry thresholds rather than relying on a single universal bilirubin cut-off.",
 "Ratify the locoregional selector and the stop/switch rules jointly with hepatobiliary and transplant surgery, hepatology, interventional radiology, radiation oncology, diagnostic radiology and medical oncology.",
 "Adopt one reading of resection in clinically significant portal hypertension and state it on the page, rather than leaving the BCLC position and the Yuan randomised result side by side for each board to choose between.",
 "Decide whether a non-invasive Baveno VIII rule-in or rule-out may stand in for HVPG when the resection decision turns on portal pressure, and make recording the criterion used, its value and its date a condition of proposing resection.",
 "Rule on whether a large spontaneous portosystemic shunt can lower measured HVPG enough to make a sub-10 mmHg value unreliable; this roadmap has not verified that concern against a primary source.",
 "Decide whether radiation segmentectomy may be offered as a definitive curative-intent option on single-arm evidence, above what tumour size it may not, and whether personalised dosimetry is required before it is described that way.",
 "Decide whether to adopt the BCLC 2026 microwave preference, distinguishing a device-specific local-control advantage from an unproven survival advantage.",
 "Decide whether this roadmap adopts the BCLC 2026 placement of external beam radiotherapy as an ablative alternative in BCLC 0 and A, given the supporting survival figures come from a retrospective multinational cohort of selected centres with no comparator arm.",
 "Agree the local AFP approach while distinguishing OPTN exception scoring (>1,000 then <500 after treatment), AASLD guidance (≥1,000) and the EASL downstaging condition (<1,000 for at least three months).",
 "Decide whether histotripsy begins as trial-only or registry-only, with credentialing, target criteria, consent language and an outcome review cadence, and require the prespecified rather than the post hoc local-control read in the registry.",
 "Adopt an explicit institutional position that TACE combined with checkpoint inhibitors is protocol-only until an overall-survival benefit is demonstrated, and record the toxicity rates the trials reported as part of the consent conversation.",
 "Decide whether any adjuvant locoregional therapy is offered after high-risk resection, recognizing that AASLD advises against neoadjuvant/adjuvant systemic therapy and EASL 2025 advises against any adjuvant treatment.",
 "Define the pre-transplant checkpoint-inhibitor washout requirement and the approval route, and confirm that local transplant policy is at least as strict as OPTN policy.",
 "Decide how SBRT bridging is selected, considering the differing nonrandomized comparative cohorts, and name who adjudicates bridging modality choice.",
 "Name who owns the response-assessment call, including which LI-RADS treatment-response algorithm applies after radiation-based therapy, and how a discordant read is resolved.",
 "Agree that the 90% and 95% quality thresholds, the one-business-day urgent triage standard and the three-procedure investigation trigger are operational judgements set for the pilot and revisable, not evidence-derived targets.",
 "Assign an owner and a calendar date for re-verifying OPTN Policy 9 criteria, drug labelling and device authorisations against this document.",
 "Pilot for 90 days, audit 20 consecutive cases, then revise before formal approval as a clinical practice guideline."
]
